```sql
-- name: top_products
-- owner: merchandising
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
-- Best sellers by units and revenue. Line items reference the variant by its
-- string id (integration feed), so it is cast when joining the catalog.
WITH selected_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       count(DISTINCT so.id)       AS order_count,
       sum(ol.quantity)            AS quantity,
       sum(ol.line_total_cents)    AS revenue_cents,
       count(DISTINCT pv.id)       AS variant_count
  FROM selected_orders so
  JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = so.id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
  JOIN products p          ON p.id = pv.product_id
 GROUP BY p.id, p.sku, p.name, p.brand, p.currency
 ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orderfilter staat nu in een aparte CTE, zodat de selectie van orders vóór de join met de regels plaatsvindt en de `orders`-tabel niet meer als volledige join hoeft mee te lopen. Het resultaat is gelijk aan het origineel: dezelfde kolommen, aggregaties en ORDER BY. De winst is waarschijnlijk beperkt, omdat de planner deze herschrijving vaak zelf al maakt.
